headline: What Are the Biggest Mistakes When Cleaning Up Smoke Damage?
articleBody: When you're dealing with smoke damage, it's easy to make mistakes that can actually worsen the problem or make restoration harder. One big one is using the wrong cleaning products. Trying to clean soot with water-based cleaners on porous surfaces like walls or fabrics will often just smear the soot, driving it deeper and making stains permanent. Another common error is not properly ventilating the area. Just closing off a room can trap the smoky odor, allowing it to penetrate further into materials. You really need to air things out thoroughly and continuously. Skipping personal protective equipment (PPE) is also a significant mistake; smoke and soot contain toxic particles that can be harmful to your lungs and skin, so masks, gloves, and eye protection are a must. Underestimating the extent of the damage is another pitfall. What looks like minor smoke residue can hide significant damage to structural elements, HVAC systems, and even electrical components, leading to long-term issues. Lastly, waiting too long to call professionals is a major misstep. The longer smoke and soot sit, the more corrosive and pervasive they become.
